item.title: Screenshotter 0.12.0
item.description:
Highlights

  • A simpler Screenshotter. Three areas, one place for each job. The left side adds things: Screenshots, Templates, Backgrounds and Elements (text, shapes and pictures in one tab). The right side changes things and is always open: whatever you've selected, or the whole design. Nothing floats over your design any more: the step bar, the starting-design sheet, the toolbar on a selection, the "Describe a change" bar and the line under the design are gone. There's one Ask AI (⌘K, with Design it for me inside) and one Export, which opens on Video when the design moves.
  • One editor. No more Edit, Animate and Preview. The design shows its finished look right on the canvas (grain, print finishes, colour grades) once you stop changing it, and the timeline is a drawer under it (⌘T). Exports stay in the editor and end with Open, Show in Finder and Copy.
  • Animate from the timeline. Every row has a + at the playhead (or right-click the row): how it comes in, keeps moving, changes or leaves, as pictures to pick from; the camera zooms in or pulls back; the background pushes, drifts or shifts colour. Each item's own settings have the same, under Animation. A design's Motion sets how it moves on its own (Still, Subtle, Float, Drift, Push in, shown on the timeline and the canvas now) and offers ready-made ways in: One by one, Lively and Tour.
  • One timeline, with your footage on it. The Footage row shows every clip of the video one after another, recordings as their frames, with the transitions between them; the + at its end adds a video or a picture. Cut a recording at the playhead (⌘B), choose the part you fumbled and delete it (⌫), or drag an end in to trim it: everything after moves up, the screen, the webcam, your voice, the cursor and the zooms together, and the export skips it too. Your recording file is never changed; ⌘Z brings a part back.
  • Pick how it starts. The start screen takes a screenshot or a recording (or records your screen, in the Mac app); once a new design's screenshot is in, eight starting designs made from it show big, once.
  • Nothing else to install. The app carries its own Node.js and ffmpeg, so designs, videos, cuts and sound work on a Mac with nothing set up. Only drawing designs still uses a Chrome-family browser you have.
  • A compact capture bar. About half as long: icons that name themselves when you point at them, the camera and microphone lime when on with a small arrow to pick one, a red dot to record, and the options (⋯) last.
  • Long lists show two rows. Wallpapers, looks, stickers, illustrations and templates each show their first rows with Show all, so the groups below stay in sight; backgrounds are three to a row.
  • Screenshotter opens on a capture bar. A bar on the screen you're using, like ⌘⇧5: a screenshot or a recording, of an area, a window or the whole screen. Open Screenshotter goes to the canvas. ⌘⇧2 or the menu bar icon brings the bar back from anywhere, over full-screen apps too.
  • Record your screen, with your camera. Turn the camera on and you're in a bubble you can drag anywhere, shape (circle, rounded, square; roundness, proportions, size, mirror, border) and turn off mid-recording, your voice carrying on. Your microphone and the Mac's own sound record too, a 3-2-1 countdown starts it, and a small pill (drag it, or shrink it to a dot) pauses, stops or throws it away.
  • Save to where you like. Screenshots and recordings each keep their own place: your library, the Desktop, any folder, or (screenshots) just the clipboard.
  • Edit recordings like Screen Studio. Stopping opens the recording with its timeline: it fills a canvas its own size, your camera is a layer of its own that stays put as the view zooms, and the video runs its full length with its sound. With Cursor effects on, the cursor is drawn by Screenshotter: smoothed, sized as you like, the right cursor for each moment, a ripple on each click. Zoom in on clicks adds zooms you can drag, change or delete, and the zoomed view follows the cursor. Every effect has its own switch in the Recording panel.
  • Every video exports fast. The Mac app draws the video on the GPU and encodes it with the media engine; the browser only draws each part of the design once (or once for each look it takes on). Recordings, device mock-ups (tilting in 3D too), text animating word by word, gentle motion, grain, colour grades, edge blur, a moving backdrop, MOV, GIF and WebM, App Store previews and videos of several shots: typically 3 to 6 times faster, and a minute of 4K in under a minute. Exports show how far along they are, and about how long is left.
  • The Screen Studio look. A recording's (or a screenshot's) Look: padding over any backdrop, rounded corners, a shadow.
  • Screenshots without a frame. Edit in Screenshotter opens a capture as a design of its own, filling a canvas its size. In the Screenshots panel, Add them chooses how new screenshots come in (in a device, with no frame, or rounded), and a design whose screenshots are frameless keeps adding them that way.
  • The timeline zooms. Stretch it out (the slider, ⌘-scroll or a pinch) to work on a long recording; it scrolls, and Fit shows it all again. Moving the camera bubble while recording now moves it in the video.
  • Edit the sound. A recording's sound is a row of its own on the timeline, its waveform drawn: drag a piece to move it, drag its ends to trim it, Cut at the playhead (⌘B) and delete what you don't want (⌫), or right-click a piece. Pieces never overlap; ← and → nudge one; one moved near where it was recorded snaps back in step. Each piece has its own volume and fades, cuts don't click, and the export plays exactly what the row shows (videos of several shots keep each shot's sound too).
  • macOS wallpapers as backdrops. The Backgrounds panel has all of Apple's: the ones on this Mac (Sonoma, the iMac colours…), and the rest download from Apple the first time you pick one (or all at once), then work offline.
  • Pretty from the start. A recording or screenshot opens with room round it (5%), rounded corners (3%) and a soft shadow, on this Mac's newest wallpaper.

Fixes

  • Zoom in on clicks is calm. The camera stays put while you click around what it already shows, goes after a click near the edge once it's been still a moment, and after one out of sight at once; a quick string of far clicks is one glide. A minute of busy clicking was 150 little nudges; it's now a handful of moves, every click still in view. Turn it off and on to redo an older recording's zooms.
  • A long recording with zooms on its clicks exports: designs can now hold thousands of animations (the export refused more than 80).
  • Your voice stays with your lips. Sound the recorder was too busy to take was dropped and the file closed up round it, pulling everything after it early (seconds out by the end of a long recording); it now keeps its time, gaps filled with silence. The last moment of what you said before Stop is kept too.
  • The editor keeps the webcam within a few hundredths of a second of the recording as it plays (it could drift a quarter of a second).
  • A round webcam stays round in a fast export (it played as a square behind its ring).
  • Starting a recording no longer freezes the bar, bubble and pill while the camera and microphone get ready; the screen and camera record in the encoder's own format, lighter on the Mac.
  • The Screenshots panel's Add them choices show their names again, and the timeline's ruler reads 1s, not 1.s.
  • The countdown says "Recording starts in", fills a ring as it runs out, and ticks (the bar's ⋯ menu turns the sound off).
